title: Remediation evidence automation and SIEM mapping (2025)
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a proposed design and practical runbook for: (1) automatic collection and storage of remediation evidence tied to vulnerability tickets, (2) a compact SIEM export schema to ingest remediation events, and (3) mapping considerations for RBAC v2 so only entitled teams can trigger evidence release. Goal is to reduce manual evidence assembly by 70% for medium/low vulns and make SRE/CS/Legal audit responses < 24h for high-severity incidents.

Context / problem statement (notes):
- Today: scanner outputs (Snyk, Trivy, Dependabot, custom image scans) land as separate tickets; engineers attach screenshots/log extracts manually. Auditors repeatedly ask for proof (patch PR, artifact hashes, rollout windows, config diffs).
- Hard problems: linking build artifacts->deployed image, partial rollouts (canary), and RBAC gating to avoid exposing sensitive logs to non-authorized viewers.
- We also need to produce consistent SIEM events so SOC can correlate "remediation completed" with alert suppression and incident closure.

Requirements (high level):
- Minimal manual steps to attach: patch PR URL, build artifact SHA, container image digest, deployment rollout id, applied config diffs, verification smoke test output (pass/fail), and timestamped operator who ran rollout.
- Evidence should be immutable and timestamped (write-once), stored in S3 with lifecycle and checksum metadata.
- SIEM export must include normalized fields for severity, CWE, CVE, affected_service, ticket_id, remediation_state, remediation_actor (principal id), and evidence_refs (array of artifact ids).
- RBAC v2 must control: who can (a) trigger automated evidence collection, (b) view raw logs attached to evidence, and (c) mark ticket as "evidence verified for audit".

Design proposal (components):
1) Remediation Evidence Collector (REC) — lightweight service that listens for ticket status transitions (ticketing system webhook) and scanner webhooks.
   - Inputs: scanner record (id, cve, severity), ticket id, PR URL, CI build metadata (pipeline id, build number, artifact shas), deployment metadata (k8s rollout id, cluster, namespaces), smoke-test output (stdout snippet), and operator principal (OID).
   - Actions: call CI/CD artifact store to fetch artifact metadata, generate evidence bundle manifest (json+sha256), push bundle to evidence-bucket (S3) under path: evidence/{ticket_id}/{bundle_ts}/{manifest}. Write-only ACLs; store pointer in ticket comment and ticket custom field evidence_url.
   - Audit log emitted for each significant step (manifest-created, artifact-pulled, evidence-uploaded, auth-check-passed).

2) SIEM Exporter — periodically exports normalized events to Splunk/Chronicle via syslog/HTTPS.
   - Event format (text schema proposal):
     event_type=remediation_event;ticket_id=SEC-4123;severity=HIGH;cve=CVE-2024-XXXX;cwe=79;affected_service=api-gateway;remediation_state=PATCH_APPLIED;remediation_actor=ava.chen;evidence_refs=[s3://evidence/evidence-bucket/SEC-4123/2025-03-12T10:22:18/manifest.json];timestamp=2025-03-12T10:22:18Z;verification=smoke_test:pass
   - Mapping notes: SIEM will consume as key=value pairs; we must avoid nested JSON arrays in the syslog line; evidence_refs will be a comma-separated list of S3 URIs.

3) RBAC v2 gating layer — integrate with internal identity/OIDC and allow policy expressions: e.g., allow(resource:ticket/evidence, action:upload) if subject.team == ticket.owner_team OR subject.has_role(security_remediation_admin).
   - UI behavior: evidence upload button shown only for entitled principals. Evidence read access will be further restricted; for external auditors a "redacted evidence export" flow must be implemented.

Ticket lifecycle (remediation-focused):
- OPEN -> TRIAGED (scanner auto-tags tentative severity) -> IN_PROGRESS (patch branch/PR created) -> PENDING_ROLLOUT (CI build and image pushed) -> ROLLING_OUT (k8s rollout id recorded) -> ROLLOUT_VERIFIED (smoke tests pass) -> EVIDENCE_CAPTURED (REC writes bundle, ticket updated) -> VERIFIED_BY_QA/SEC -> CLOSED

Patch SLA suggestions (working):
- CRITICAL (CVSS >= 9 or active exploit): patch + test + canary deploy within 48 hours, full rollout within 7 days. Evidence bundle required within 24 hours of PENDING_ROLLOUT.
- HIGH (7 <= CVSS < 9): patch within 7 days, rollout within 21 days. Evidence bundle required before VERIFIED_BY_QA.
- MEDIUM: review within 14 days, patch or accepted risk within 30 days. Evidence bundle at close.
- LOW: monitor; evidence optional unless requested.

Automation rules / heuristics (notes):
- If scanner output contains "fix PR": auto-scan ticket for PR URL; if found, REC will poll CI until artifact SHA appears, then create evidence bundle automatically.
- For image vulnerabilities (OS packages): collect image manifest + package-lock + SBOM (if available). If SBOM missing, enqueue SBOM generation job (small blocker).
- For infra-as-code vulns: capture git diff for IaC PR and terraform plan/apply output.

Evidence bundle manifest example (thin):
- manifest_id: eb-20250312-0001
- ticket_id: SEC-4123
- timestamp: 2025-03-12T10:22:18Z
- artifacts: [artifact:ci:build-555:sha=abcd1234, artifact:container:sha=sha256:... , smoke_test:status=pass, rollout_id=k8s-rollout-293]
- signature: sha256:... (REC signs manifest with service key)

Operational concerns / open questions (TODO):
- Where do we store the private key for REC signing in Private deployments? KMS/HSM integration required; map to Private product offering.
- Retention policy: auditors want 3 years for some customers; S3 lifecycle/config required and separate retention flag for enterprise customers.
- RBAC: how granular should evidence visibility be? per-ticket, per-bundle, per-field? Need legal input for exported redaction rules.
- SIEM quotas: sample event size must remain < 32KB to avoid ingestion issues. Evidence_refs lists must be constrained.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): small prototype REC that listens to ticket webhooks and accepts manual attachments. Create PoC SIEM event into dev Splunk. Demo internal.
- Phase 1 (4–6 weeks): integrate with CI (Buildkite/GH actions) to pull artifact metadata, auto-generate manifests, upload to evidence-bucket. Add minimal RBAC checks.
- Phase 2 (4 weeks): add SBOM collection flows, IaC diff capture, and more robust signing/KMS. Integrate with SIEM production endpoint and alert suppression hooks.
- Phase 3 (ongoing): enterprise features: per-customer retention, legal redaction exports, and on-prem REC packaging.

Acceptance criteria (initial):
- REC can produce an evidence bundle for an automated PR-based fix end-to-end in < 30 minutes from PR merge (dev env).
- SIEM receives remediation_event with evidence_refs and remediation_state transitions for a sample set of 10 tickets.
- RBAC v2 policy checks prevent non-entitled users from downloading raw log attachments in a test matrix.

Quick checklist (actionable next steps):
- [ ] Get legal/ops input on retention and redaction requirements (assign: Leah)
- [ ] Add ticket custom fields for evidence_url and evidence_manifest_id in ticketing system (assign: Marcus)
- [ ] Spike on KMS integration and signing approach (assign: Derek)
- [ ] Prepare demo for Security+SRE sync on 2025-04-09

Notes to self / working thoughts:
- Keep evidence bundles minimal (manifest + pointers) — avoid filling SIEM with large payloads.
- For private deployments, offer a connector that writes to customer S3; don't ship secrets.
- Consider future: integrate with audit-log schema so system-level audit events link to evidence bundle manifests (e.g., audit_event: evidence_downloaded -> include manifest_id and principal).

Related docs and references:
- Confluence: /display/Sec/Remediation+Lifecycle+Design (link above)
- Ticket: JIRA-SEC-4123 (remediation lifecycle epic)
- Infra PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/879 (CI artifact metadata changes)

Unresolved:
- Need list of scanners to prioritize for first pass (Snyk, Trivy, Clair, Dependabot, internal image-scan).
- Decide on canonical evidence manifest schema (tight vs extensible).

End of working doc.

(Informal: this is intentionally rough — aim to use the Phase 0 PoC to learn, not ship perfect schema first time)
